narrative:
Advisory Note: Students should declare their major, degree (BA or BFA) and concentration by winter quarter of junior year. Deadline does not apply to students in the directing concentration. Students can update their concentration choice if requirements can be completed by graduation quarter.
MAJOR REGULATIONSPREREQUISITES Check the General Catalog for the prerequisites to all listed courses.
P/NP GRADING OPTION Not allowed for major courses (prep or UD major).
SUBSTITUTIONS In the major requirements permissible only by petition to the department chair and dean.
G.P.A REQUIREMENTS At least 2.0 overall UC average in all upper-division major courses and all courses (Prep and UD) for the major.
DOUBLE MAJORS With the approval of each department chairperson, up to a total of 8 units may be applied simultaneously to both UD majors.

nodes.title: Fundamentals of Choreography
nodes.description: A study of the basic elements pertaining to the craft of choreography. Emphasis on exploration of movement variation, breath rhythm, the development of dance phrases, and the use of stage space. For dance majors.

nodes.title: Improvisation
nodes.description: The fundamental exploration of movement potential with particular focus on the individual and group dynamics.

nodes.title: Modern Dance I
nodes.description: Analysis and exploration of the technical aspects of movement as an expressive medium. For dance majors.

nodes.title: Digital Editing for Dance
nodes.description: A video skill-building course that introduces students to non-linear editing software and video camera operation. Drawing upon choreographic principles, students will create short film projects expanding their compositional proficiency and their technical knowledge of video editing tools.

nodes.title: Embodied Anatomy
nodes.description: For dancers and individuals interested in studying human anatomy from a dancer's perspective, including scientific information, experiential practice, and a focus on both the body's physical structure and its kinetic possibilities. Brings awareness to how we synthesize time and space in order to move rhythmically, create coherent shapes, locomote through space and organize complex coordination of multiple systems within the body. Anatomical awareness helps with injury prevention and offers one a more meaningful relationship to their human form.

nodes.title: Play Analysis
nodes.description: Deep study of key concepts used in the analysis of plays in performance, including story, action, genre, liveness, and experience. Includes study of exemplary plays and performances.

nodes.title: Performance in Global Contexts: Africa and the Caribbean
nodes.description: Introduction to local performance traditions in Africa and the Caribbean, such as storytelling, ritual, and Carnival. The course also examines how African and Caribbean playwrights put those traditions to social and political uses by incorporating them into post-colonial plays.

nodes.title: Performance in Global Contexts: ASIA
nodes.description: This course surveys a range of Asian performances across a diversity of locations, from the traditional theater forms of Japanese Kabuki, Indonesian Wayang Kulit, and Indian Kathakali to modern forms in India and Japan to contemporary Chinese performance art. Theater forms like Chinese Jingju and Japanese Noh will prompt us to reevaluate what the performer does in rehearsal and in situations on and off the stage. By exploring recent modern and contemporary performance forms, we will reassess how an actor, dancer, or puppeteer can challenge the status quo and effect change. As we ask these questions, we will situate Asian performance within social, political, and historical contexts to understand its rich functions and significances.

nodes.title: Performance in Global Contexts: EUROPE
nodes.description: Introduction to theater and performance practice and traditions in Europe. Topics will include ritual, the rise of a public theater, the political uses of theater, the development of festival theater, and the uses of performance in non-theatrical contexts.

nodes.title: Introduction To Acting
nodes.description: An introduction for majors and nonmajors to the multiple problems of the actor's art and craft.

nodes.title: Introduction to Dramatic Writing
nodes.description: A intensive introduction to playwriting for beginning dramatists. Students will read and analyze the structure of plays, write and stage their own short plays, and gain experience acting in and directing each other's work. Homework for the course includes a series of written and performance-based assignments.

nodes.title: Design Fundamentals for Dance and Theater
nodes.description: In this course, you will be introduced to the fundamentals of design for theatre, dance, performance, and live events. You’ll be taught about four disciplines of design including Scenery, Costume, Lighting, and Projection along with a series of approaches to formulate and communicate your own design work to others. Inspired by texts, music, and research, you will create visual designs that express ideas and aesthetic choices while fulfilling practical requirements for the performer or participant in an intentional environment. Through hands-on projects and class activities, you will create designs for live performance through writing, research, 2D media and 3D models.

nodes.title: Scenic Design
nodes.description: Projects in the interpretation of plays through scenic elements with concentration on the design process and the dramatic use of space. Drafting projects including floor plans, elevations and basic perspective drawing.

nodes.title: Stage Lighting Design
nodes.description: Lecture-demonstration in instrumentation, color in light, control equipment, and basic lighting design theories. Technical drawing including light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design. Some practical application through laboratory and studio exercise.

nodes.title: Projection Design
nodes.description: Exploration of basic elements and principles of projection design for live performance. Projects in the interpretation of plays through visual elements. Introduction to projection, video, and media design for live performance and installation. Projects involve interpretation of plays and music, technical approaches to equipment, and programming equipment for media designs.

nodes.title: Costume Design
nodes.description: In this course students will receive a more detailed, but introductory exposure to the world of costume design. They will learn how costume design plays an essential function in the collaboration of live theatre, opera, television, and film. Students will experience the step-by-step creative process of this design discipline, while implementing strong character analysis skills and recognizing the importance of thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to build characters, from the ground up, using the power of dress.

nodes.title: Scenic Practicum
nodes.description: Empirical understanding of methods of assembly and materials for stage scenery. Shop organization and operation are experienced during the construction process.

nodes.title: Lighting Practicum
nodes.description: Empirical understanding of optical properties of lightin units, available hanging positions and apparatus, lighting control, electrical safety and stage crew organization.

nodes.title: Costume Practicum
nodes.description: Empirical understanding of methods of assembly and materials for stage dress. Costume shop organization and operation are experienced during the construction process.

nodes.title: Run Crew Practicum
nodes.description: Empirical understanding of backstage organization and operation during live performance.

nodes.title: Theater Games
nodes.description: Using theater games, improvisation and storytelling, this course expands the imagination and frees the instincts of the actor. Exercises reflect the work of improvisation icons such as Viola Spolin, Augusto Boal, and Paul Sills. Students also explore techniques for sharing/teaching these games in community settings such as schools, senior citizen centers, etc. Prerequisite: Theater 5 or Instructor's Approval. Highly recommended for students focusing on Theater and Community.

nodes.title: Theater Workshop
nodes.description: Projects in costume, scenery, lighting, acting, directing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Stage Management
nodes.description: Foundational course exploring the full range of duties and responsibilities of a stage manager, a vital role for all theatrical and dance productions.

nodes.title: Playwriting Workshop
nodes.description: An exploration of the essential components of playwriting. Exercises focus on writing dialogue, monologue, creating three-dimensional characters, building effective story structures, and developing action through language and stage images. A series of written assignments.

nodes.title: Advanced Playwriting Workshop
nodes.description: A continued exploration of the essential components of playwriting. Writing exercises in dialogue, monologue, character, story structure, action and stage images. Students focus on developing their individual writing voice. A series of written assignments.

nodes.title: Collaboration & Ensemble Devising
nodes.description: Open to playwrights, dancers, directors, actors, and designers. A series of written and ensemble performance-based assignments in which small groups explore different ways of generating and staging new material.

nodes.title: Design Critical Studies
nodes.description: This course introduces advanced design and directing students to key concepts and skills that promote successful theatrical collaboration. Directing and design teams will research all aspects of a play and develop a proposed unified production using a shared verbal and visual language.

nodes.title: Advanced Scenic Design
nodes.description: This course builds upon tools learned in THTR 22: Beginning Set Design to increase fluency in scenic design approaches and techniques. Focusing on building ideas from texts and music, you will evolve design approaches through research and critiques. Designs will culminate in scale models and supporting materials. Projects in THTR 122 will focus on opera, dance, and musical theatre with unique scenic demands including multiple locations, period detail, and awareness of performance styles and conventions.

nodes.title: Advanced Stage Lighting Design
nodes.description: Lecture-demonstration of controllable properties and functions of light. Includes technical drawing: light plots, scheduling and organization for lighting design, drawing using light and shadow, perspective drawing. Practical application through studio exercise.

nodes.title: Design Portfolio
nodes.description: This course will introduce students to advanced topics in the art and craft of visual media design for projection and video with an emphasis on live performance.

nodes.title: Advanced Costume Design
nodes.description: In this course students will receive an advance and detailed perspective on the art of costume design. Through four different projects, they will explore different character development experiences, with a continued focus on thematic storytelling. Together, students will learn how to craft character, while focusing on the scope of a full production.

nodes.title: Theatre Rendering Techniques
nodes.description: Advanced theatre rendering techniques for the theatre designer. Continued development in drawing and use of different mediums. Concentration on rendering light, shadow, and texture.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES

nodes.title: History of Decorative Styles
nodes.description: A survey of the evolution of design styles and production trends in western theater, emphasizing the history of design and designers, including a study of both interior and exterior decoration with concentration on furnishing, accessories and the changing patterns of culture.

nodes.title: Puppet Design and Construction
nodes.description: Explores the history of various puppet styles and will focus on the design and creation of three iconic puppet forms: Thai shadow puppets (Nang yai), rod puppets (Bunraku), and marionettes. Students will learn both the mechanical aspects and the artistic design elements of puppet creation by creating one of each of these three styles.

nodes.title: Advanced Acting Workshop I
nodes.description: Advanced exploration, performances, and criticism of scenes from a broad range of dramatic scripts with focus on the actor's perspective.

nodes.title: Advanced Acting Workshop II
nodes.description: Further exploration of performances and criticism of scenes from a broad range of dramatic scripts with focus on the actor's perspective.

nodes.title: I.V. Live
nodes.description: This course produces a weekly performance series in Isla Vista. Students get first-hand experience in the rigors of theatrical production, as they learn to execute all logistical, technical and promotional details. The course is affiliated with Isla Vista Arts.

nodes.title: The People's Voice
nodes.description: Students and teens from the community collaborate in writing, crafting, and performing an epic myth through the lens of their personal stories.

nodes.title: Shakespeare Production
nodes.description: Students study, rehearse and produce one of Shakespeare's plays. The class culminates with performances that are open to the public during the final week. Students can participate as actors, assistant directors, designers or stage managers.

nodes.title: Shakespeare Production
nodes.description: Students study, rehearse and produce one of Shakespeare's plays. The class culminates with performances that are open to the public during the final week. Students can participate as actors, assistant directors, designers or stage managers.

nodes.title: Launch Pad: New Plays in Process
nodes.description: Working with the artistic director of LAUNCH PAD and 3 professional playwrights, this 3-week intensive course workshops a new play every week. Student actors, directors, designers, dramaturgs, playwrights, and stage managers learn the vital skills of working on new plays in the earliest stages of their development. The workshop culminates in an invited public reading at the end of each week. Over the 3 weeks, participants have the opportunity to take on different functions in the process.

nodes.title: Theatre Workshop
nodes.description: Projects in costume, scenery, lighting, acting, directing.

nodes.title: Introduction to Stage Directing
nodes.description: Basic principles of directing. Lectures, demonstrations, and small practical projects offer the non-specialist and potential directing concentration student a broad understanding of the directorial process.

nodes.title: Techniques of Directing
nodes.description: Laboratory in directorial scene work. Students take on scenes from contemporary plays. Focus is on text analysis, visual storytelling, and collaboration with actors.

nodes.title: Advanced Directing
nodes.description: Advanced directing techniques and scene work, including departures from realism. Students also learn about collaboration with designers.

nodes.title: Directorial Production
nodes.description: Full directorial responsibility for the mounting of a one-act play.

nodes.title: Projects in Directing
nodes.description: Full directorial responsibility for the mounting of a second one-act play or other special project.

nodes.title: Projects in Design and Production
nodes.description: Special projects in each area of concentration.

nodes.title: Applied Theater/The Artist as Activist - Basics
nodes.description: The Artist as Activist Basics introduces the student to the fundamentals of Applied Theater through examination of theory, history and imagining as a preparation for application and fieldwork. The course prepares the student to implement a project in the community. The project can be teaching or performance based. In addition to developing as researchers and theater activists, students will learn about the producing, promotional and ethical dimensions of self-starting a Theater & Community initiative.

nodes.title: American Drama to 1940
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: History of the American drama and theater from early years to 1940. Important plays, performers, institutions, and styles of production are given selective attention.

nodes.title: American Drama 1940 to Present
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: History of the American drama and theater from 1940 to the present. Important plays, performers, institutions, and styles of production are given selective attention.

nodes.title: Contemporary American Drama and Theater
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: Close study of major playwrights, directors, solo performance artists, and other artists working in the contemporary American theater, mainstream and avant-garde. Writing assignments focus on developing critical arguments about new work.

nodes.title: Latin American Theater and Performance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: Survey of Hispanic-American drama and theory including authors like Carballido, Gambaro, Marques, Triana, Valdez, and others.

nodes.title: Culture Clash: Studies in U.S. Latino Theater
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: A survey, in English, of the dramatic literature of U.S. Latinos from 1965 to the present. Includes history and criticism of the theater of Chicano, Puerto Rican, Cuban, and other Americans of Hispanic origin in the U.S.

nodes.title: Asian American Theater
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: Overview of Asian American theater and its political and artistic achievements, from foundational Asian American theater companies and playwrights to contemporary performance artists. Issues addressed include race and ethnicity, gender and sexuality, and intergenerational conflict.

nodes.title: Race, Gender, and Performance
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: Comparative analysis of contemporary American plays and performances by artists of diverse gender, sexual, ethnic, and racial backgrounds. Students learn to perceive and critically respond to race and gender issues in plays and the theatrical production.

nodes.description: Special topics in British theater and drama.

Through the lens of performance studies, this class asks how athletic and sporting bodies reinforce, disrupt, or complicate dominant cultural and social narratives.

groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: Through creative arts practices, analysis, workshops and new performance, this course explores processes of transformation and translation of traces of memories and experiences into provocative art works. Experimental performance practices encompass theatrical, movement based, sonic, music-based and visual arts.

nodes.title: Sport as Performance: The Climbing Body in Theater and Film
groups: UPPER-DIVISION MAJOR: THEATER AND PERFORMANCE STUDIES
nodes.description: Explores rock climbing and mountaineering as performance in theater and documentary film. Classes consist of lectures, guest speakers, film viewing, and discussion where we interrogate what it means to be a performer in a sport like climbing. In looking at climbers of different lived experiences, this class offers new understandings of the study of sport through performance, how the climbing body informs our understanding of the role of the actor, and how the performing body disrupts or upholds dominant cultural and social narratives.

nodes.description: An investigation of Shakespeare's plays through the media of performance; viewing of Shakespearean productions on film and videotape, in calssroom rehearsal, and in stage performances as available; reading and critical analysis of selected Shakespearean plays.

nodes.title: Principles of Stage Management
nodes.description: Upper division course that builds upon the foundational information of THTR 95, providing a greater depth and breadth of exploration into the duties of the stage manager from pre-production through strike. Topics include communication, organizational skills, rehearsal procedures, and performance responsibilities. Greater stage management practical experience gained through in-class exercises and outside assignments.

nodes.title: Stage Management Practicum
nodes.description: Production oriented course allowing student practical experience in stage management training. Student will serve as assistant stage manager or stagemanager for a main stage or student directed departmental production.

nodes.title: Dance Production
nodes.prereq_text: Theater 19; 22 or 123 or 125; upper-division standing; consent of instructor.
nodes.description: Exploration of the process of collaboration between dance choreographers and theater designers in the development of designs for dance productions. Final project is a public performance of the choreographers' and designer' work.
